engine.name: A.B.E. — American Butterfly Effect
engine.type: Constitutional Capital Discovery, Recovery, and Deployment Engine
engine.author: Terra Dawn Shouse
engine.mission: Identify constrained capital flow, measure divergence from governing authority, quantify recoverable value, model lawful deployment pathways, and verify post-deployment stability through deterministic, local-only execution.

core_principles.constitutional_first: Start from the Constitution and governing framework before moving to statutes, regulations, funding conditions, state law, agency policy, and practice.
core_principles.hierarchy_of_authority: Constitution → federal authority → funding conditions → state law → agency practice.
core_principles.public_data_preference: Use public law, regulations, funding tables, public reports, and transparent assumptions whenever possible.
core_principles.local_execution: User documents and artifacts must be processed client-side in the browser unless the user knowingly chooses otherwise.
core_principles.non_commercial: The engine is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 and must remain a public-good framework, not a privatized SaaS product or paywalled tool.
core_principles.human_first: The engine evaluates systems, laws, policies, funding uses, and institutional practices. It does not score people.
core_principles.plain_language: Every technical output should have a plain-language explanation so citizens are not required to become experts to understand results.
core_principles.determinism: Identical inputs and model settings should produce identical outputs.
core_principles.auditability: All major outputs should be structured, inspectable, and exportable with integrity receipts where possible.

privacy_model.data_flow: User uploads, pasted text, and structured inputs are processed locally through the Intake layer and written into local artifacts. Downstream modules read those artifacts locally.
privacy_model.external_transmission: A.B.E. must not silently send user documents, artifacts, or analysis outputs to external APIs, servers, or third-party tools.
privacy_model.artifacts: Major modules produce structured JSON or CSV outputs. Integrity modules may generate SHA-256 hashes to support chain-of-custody and tamper detection.
privacy_model.ai_boundary: External AI assistants may help interpret, explain, draft, or summarize only when clearly identified as external to the A.B.E. engine. A.B.E. itself remains local-first.
privacy_model.user_control: Users control whether they download, share, or submit artifacts.

citizen_first_flow.goal: A user should be able to upload once, run the full engine, and receive a plain-language report plus audit-ready artifacts.
simple_flow: 1. Start Here — User reads a simple explanation of what A.B.E. does.
2. Intake — User uploads a file, pastes text, or enters structured facts.
3. Classification — Engine identifies the domain and relevant authority path.
4. Constitutional / authority analysis — Engine maps the facts against governing authority and flags divergence signals.
5. Economic impact — Engine estimates recoverable value, deployment capacity, and macroeconomic effect.
6. Results — Engine displays plain-language findings and key numbers.
7. Receipt — Engine produces structured JSON and integrity artifacts for audit or review.
8. Advanced views — Users, lawyers, auditors, researchers, or analysts may inspect individual modules.
citizen_first_flow.user_visible_flow: Upload → Run Full Pipeline → Read Plain-Language Results → Download Audit JSON

INTAKE.name: Document Intake + OCR Bridge
INTAKE.purpose: Normalize user documents, pasted text, and structured inputs into a local artifact.
INTAKE.citizen_view: Upload or paste once. The engine prepares the input for analysis.

CAE.name: Constitutional Alignment Engine
CAE.purpose: Establish baseline alignment conditions before divergence is measured.
CAE.citizen_view: Checks whether the right authority path is being used.

CDA.name: Constitutional Divergence Analyzer
CDA.purpose: Transform facts into structured divergence signals.
CDA.citizen_view: Finds where the situation may not match the governing authority.

CDI.name: Constitutional Divergence Index
CDI.purpose: Measure divergence using a normalized score.
CDI.plain_language: How far did the system drift?

CIRI.name: Constitutional Integrity ROI Engine
CIRI.purpose: Convert measured divergence into recoverable capital and return-on-alignment estimates.

CIBS.name: Constitutional Integrity Baseline Schema
CIBS.purpose: Allocate recovery capital into structured categories.

CII.name: Constitutional Integrity Index
CII.purpose: Measure whether allocation propagates into real system improvement.

INTEGRATION.name: Audit & SHA-256 Integrity Layer
INTEGRATION.purpose: Bind module outputs into a local audit receipt.
INTEGRATION.plain_language: Did the chain stay consistent and verifiable?

MACRO.name: Macroeconomic Cascade Model
MACRO.purpose: Project broader economic effects across sectors or jurisdictions.
MACRO.plain_language: What is the larger economic ripple effect?

RT.name: Rebuild Together Engine
RT.purpose: Deploy recovery capital into Capital Activation Sectors and estimate activation value.
RT.plain_language: How does recovered value become real-world deployment?

CFF.name: Constitutional Funding Forensics
CFF.purpose: Analyze funding flow and allocation patterns against authority and program scope.
CFF.plain_language: Is funding aligned with the purpose it was provided for?

CCRI.name: Consumer Credit Risk Integrity
CCRI.purpose: Evaluate credit participation and financial access constraints.
CCRI.plain_language: How does the system affect access to credit and participation?

AFFE.name: Appropriation Fidelity Funding Engine
AFFE.purpose: Measure post-deployment stability using RT, CII, and Integration outputs.
AFFE.plain_language: Did deployment create stable forward movement?

LAW.name: Authority Layer
LAW.purpose: Store structured constitutional, statutory, regulatory, and funding authority references.

DOCTRINE.name: Framework Mapping Layer
DOCTRINE.purpose: Store doctrine maps, rule-of-law principles, and framework references.

LEARN.name: Guided Engine Learning Interface
LEARN.purpose: Explain the engine in plain language and guide users through the correct flow.

SYSTEM.name: Command Interface & Execution Layer
SYSTEM.purpose: Run the full pipeline and display plain-language results plus audit JSON.

ENGINE_CORE.name: Classification & Validity Layer
ENGINE_CORE.purpose: Provide pre-execution classification, validity checks, law-pack routing, and supporting audit logic.

doctrine_summary.constitutional_hierarchy: Constitution → federal statutes → federal regulations → funding conditions → state law → agency practice.
doctrine_summary.plain_language_rule: Government action should be measured against the authority that permits it, the limits placed on that authority, and the funding conditions tied to the action.
void_ab_initio_conditions: Removes or nullifies a guaranteed remedy
Transfers power from the people to government without amendment
Creates penalties for exercising a right
Invents powers not delegated in the governing framework

transportation_scope_seed.purpose: Support future DOT / FMCSA / MCSAP law-pack analysis.
core_questions: Is the person acting in commerce?
Is the vehicle commercial or private?
Does the vehicle meet federal motor carrier scope thresholds?
Is hazardous material requiring placarding involved?
Which agency has lawful authority over the action?
Which funding program supports the enforcement activity?
Are state practices aligned with federal funding conditions and statutory scope?
transportation_scope_seed.plain_language_goal: A user should understand the difference between private movement and regulated commercial transportation without needing to read the entire USC/CFR stack.
